subject: Multiplexed inference rightsizing assessment and NIC-level egress planning
messages:
From: Alice Morris <alice.morris@enterprisedata.ai>

Cc: sre-lead@finserv.co

Subject: Right-sizing for multiplexed private pool (throughput + NIC planning)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this — we're kicking off the architecture review for our private deployment with Redwood. High level: we expect to run multi-tenant multiplexed inference across a VPC-connected on-prem GPU cluster. Key asks:

- Peak sustained concurrency: ~120 rps (inference requests), typical request sizes ~512 tokens, burst to 250 rps for 2–3 minute windows.
- Preferred models: mixture of 13B and 70B variants; quantized replicas expected for cost reasons.
- Requirement: <200 ms P95 latency for short-chat paths, best-effort for long generation.
- Networking constraint: site egress cap 10 Gbps; want guidance on NIC placement, bonding, and whether to carve per-tenant egress budgets.

I've attached a profiling spreadsheet with request mix and a sample streaming workload. Could your team recommend a sizing baseline (GPU counts, NIC arrangement, warm-pool margin) and call out failure modes we should design against?

Cheers,
Alice
Infrastructure Eng, EnterpriseData.ai

Hi Alice — thanks for the detail and the attachments, that's perfect. I'm looping in Jonas (runtime sizing) and Vanessa (network/ops) to fold in the production constraints.

Initial thoughts up front:
- We should treat the workload as "mixed-length streaming + short chat". That means bandwidth and per-token compute both matter.
- For 120 rps sustained at avg 512 tokens, you're looking at roughly 61k tokens/sec steady-state (120 * 512 / 1s). Bursts to 250 rps pushes tokens/sec ~128k.
- Primary sizing levers: GPU model family (13B vs 70B), quantization level (int8/4), batching window, and KV cache hit rate for repeated prefixes.

Next steps: Jonas will produce a baseline GPU fleet configuration (counts / model mix / warm-pool) and Vanessa will produce NIC/egress layout options that fit under 10 Gbps and support graceful overload.

—Hannah

Subject: RE: Right-sizing for multiplexed private pool (throughput + NIC planning)

Hi all — dug into the spreadsheet and the streaming sample. Below is a conservative baseline and the assumptions.

Assumptions:
- 13B quantized instances: avg token latency ~1.5 ms/token on A100-40GB with our optimized kernels; 70B quantized: ~3.5 ms/token.
- Typical request pattern: 40% short-chat (<64 tokens), 45% medium (~256 tokens), 15% long/streaming (512+ tokens).
- Effective batch efficiency (multiplexing across concurrent requests) ~2x for chat patterns, ~1.2x for streaming-heavy flows.
- KV cache hit: expect 10–20% for repeated prefixes; improves throughput marginally.

Baseline fleet (targeting sustained 120 rps / burst 250 rps):
- Option A (mixed model): 8x A100-40GB hosts running 2x 13B quantized replicas + 1x 70B quantized replica each (total model replicas: 16x13B, 8x70B). Warm pool: 20% additional capacity (cold start buffer).
- Option B (13B-heavy, cost optimized): 12x A100-40GB hosts running 3x 13B replicas each (36x13B) — higher concurrency, lower P95 for short chat. Warm pool: 15%.

Estimated throughput headroom (steady, post batching):
- Option A: supports ~140–160 rps steady with 20% warm headroom; bursts to ~300 rps for 3–4 minutes if admission control is lenient.
- Option B: supports ~180–220 rps steady; burstable to ~350 rps with warmed replicas.

NIC / network notes that affect sizing:
- Each A100 host with high utilization can push ~8–10 Gbps egress depending on tokenization and chunking for streaming responses. If you colocate 8 hosts behind a single 10 Gbps uplink, you risk saturating during bursts.
- Prefer 2x10Gb uplinks with active/standby or LACP and per-host egress policing by tenant to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbour.

Failure modes to plan for:
- Egress saturation: prioritize short-chat requests and shed/queue long-streaming flows when egress > 8 Gbps.
- Cold start during model reloads: keep a small warm pool and prefetch KV cache for hottest tenants.
- High connection churn: ensure edge proxies keep connection pooling and token batching windows adaptive to request mix.

I'll attach a short sizing workbook with per-replica throughput numbers in the shared Drive.

-Jonas
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Quick operational guidance on NIC and egress patterns:

1) Uplink topology options (ranked):
   - Preferred: 2x10Gb LACP per rack, with per-host bandwidth policing (tc/ebtables) and per-tenant shaping at the ToR. This gives graceful degradation under bursts.
   - Alternate: 4x1Gb per host with link aggregation — avoid unless host-level CPU can handle the aggregation overhead.

2) Bonding and isolation:
   - Use VLANs per tenant plus macvlan for strict isolation. Egress policing rules applied at the ToR for tenant-level caps.

3) Monitoring and SLOs:
   - Export host NIC counters and per-socket egress metrics to the Redwood Console. Create dashboards for host-level token/sec, egress-Gbps, and queue length.

4) Immediate recommendations for EnterpriseData.ai cluster under a 10 Gbps site cap:
   - Spread hosts across two separate 10G uplinks and tag tenants with egress budgets. For Option A (8 hosts), dedicate 5 hosts to uplink-A and 3 to uplink-B; configure dynamic rebalancing for sustained >70% utilization.

I'll prepare a short runbook for traffic-shedding policies and include example tc rules.

—Vanessa
Sr. Network Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is really actionable. A few clarifying points from our SRE lead (cc'd earlier):
- We can budget 1.5 Gbps per tenant during steady-state and allow burst sharing up to the site cap. We'll want explicit tenant caps enforced by ToR.
- Regarding the model mix: we prefer Option B if it simplifies operational monitoring and reduces P95 tail for short-chat flows.

Can you produce an explicit host-by-host plan (which host runs which replicas), and a short traffic-shedding policy we can hand to our Network team? If possible, also call out the expected ops cost (rough host-hour estimate) and a short list of runbook play actions for an egress saturation event.

Cheers,
Alice
